title: The Hudson Valley market this autumn
excerpt: Prices are steady, homes are selling in about three weeks, and there are more buyers than houses under $500,000.
content:
Here's what we're seeing across the valley this season.

Prices

Steady in most towns, and still rising a little in Rhinebeck and Hudson.

Speed

Homes priced well are selling in about three weeks.

Buyers

More buyers than houses under $500,000, so those go quickly.

title: Buying your first home: a checklist
excerpt: From a mortgage letter to the final walk-through. Everything first-time buyers ask Ana about.
content:
Buying your first home is a lot of steps. Here they are in order.

Before you look

Get a letter from a lender, so sellers take your offer seriously.

When you find one

Make an offer with an inspection, and keep some money aside for surprises.

Before you close

Walk through the house again the day before, and check everything works.

title: Which repairs pay for themselves before you sell
excerpt: Paint, yes. A new kitchen, usually not. What Claire tells sellers before they spend a dollar.
content:
Most sellers spend too much on the wrong things. Here's what pays.

Worth doing

Fresh paint, a tidy garden and fixing anything that drips or sticks.

Usually not

New kitchens and bathrooms rarely earn back what they cost.

Ask first

We'll walk round with you and tell you honestly.

title: Moving up from the city: what to know
excerpt: Commutes, winters, internet and schools. The questions we hear most from buyers leaving New York.
content:
Every week someone calls from the city. These are their questions.

The commute

Hudson and Rhinebeck have trains; Woodstock is better for working from home.

Winter

Ask about heating costs and who plows the road.

Internet

Check before you offer. Most villages have fiber; some lanes don't.
